records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which name leads. NC State's Common Name(s) list (American Boneset, Boneset, Bonset, Feverwort, Thoroughwort) is alphabetized, not ranked, but its first entry is 'American Boneset'; Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated Common Name field reads 'Common Name: American boneset' and RHS's page subtitle reads 'American boneset.' The plain name leads elsewhere: Penn State Extension's page is titled 'Rain Garden Plants: Boneset,' NC State's own Description opens 'Boneset is a large herbaceous, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial herb in the aster (Asteraceae) family,' and MOBOT's Noteworthy Characteristics opens 'Eupatorium perfoliatum, commonly called boneset.' 'Thoroughwort' appears as an alternate name in NC State's list and in MOBOT's 'Also commonly called thoroughwort.'
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's "Poisonous to Humans" block rates this species Low severity: "It causes vomiting and has a laxative effect laxative in large doses. May cause dermatitis. Potential for liver damage if used long-term. Drying the plant parts helps to decrease toxins." Its Poison Toxic Principle is listed as pyrrolizidine alkaloids, and the page's Causes Contact Dermatitis field is answered Yes. The full Poison Part list, reproduced without truncation, is Flowers, Leaves, Seeds and Stems, each listed as its own item. This severity rating and symptom list come from NC State's human-scoped "Poisonous to Humans" heading; the page carries no separate Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tags for this species, so no cat/dog-specific toxicity claim is supported by it. NC State's separate Edibility field calls the plant "Toxic and bitter," and Missouri Botanical Garden's Noteworthy Characteristics states "All parts of the plant are quite toxic and bitter."
unknowns: toxic_to_pets left null: NC State's toxicity content is headed 'Poisonous to Humans' with no Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tags for this species, and no other admissible source (Missouri Botanical Garden, RHS, Penn State Extension, or the other admissible domains) was found addressing cat- or dog-specific toxicity for Eupatorium perfoliatum, so this field is left null per the strict cat/dog scoping rule rather than inferred from the human-scoped data.
humidity_need, humidity_pct_min, humidity_pct_max left null: no admissible source discusses ambient humidity for this outdoor wetland perennial.
light_fc_min and light_fc_good left null: no admissible source gives foot-candle light figures for this species.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: NC State's '6 or more hours' (Full sun) and '2-6 hours' (Partial Shade) figures are part of its site-wide Light category legend, not species-specific prose, so per the rules they cannot be used; RHS and Penn State Extension give no hour figures either.

outdoor_sun_exposure limited to full_sun and part_shade: none of NC State's, RHS's, or Penn State Extension's structured or prose sun fields for this species supported part_sun or full_shade values, so those were excluded.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State does not list a Soil pH field for this species, and RHS's structured pH field reads 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' with alkaline explicitly acceptable, so no numeric ceiling or floor can be set.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note left null: no admissible source gives day/night temperature ranges or a stated chill-damage onset temperature for this species; only USDA hardiness zones (3-9, a survival rating) were found, which per the rules is not a substitute for an onset figure.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, and water_estimate_basis left null: this is an in-ground perennial and no admissible source frames its watering in terms of a dry-down target, check depth, or day intervals.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength left null: no admissible source discusses fertilizing this species.

soil_drainage lands moderate. NC State's structured Soil Drainage field, the field this catalog reads first, carries Good Drainage alongside Moist (plus Occasional Flooding and Occasionally Wet), and RHS's species-page Moisture field reads 'Moist but well–drained or Poorly–drained'; NC State's own Description puts the cultivation range at 'average, medium to wet soils with a consistent water source,' and Missouri Botanical Garden's structured field reads 'Water: Medium to wet.' The wet-end evidence is Penn State Extension's rain-garden Site Conditions labels ('Soil: Clay and sandy, needs constant moisture', 'Hydrologic zones: Wet/moist') and its description sentence 'Tolerates flooded conditions well.' A rain-garden siting label is not a cultivation drainage requirement in this catalog, and a flood tolerance is a tolerance rather than a requirement, so the wet-end evidence is disclosed here rather than driving the field to moisture_retentive. RHS's Moisture field and its Cultivation sentence ('Grow in any moist soil in full sun or partial shade') are species-page text: RHS keeps its genus-generic prose in a separate, labelled Genus field, so they are weighed as species evidence.

RHS's genus-level Genus field text ("Eupatorium can be annuals, herbaceous perennials, subshrubs or evergreen shrubs...") was not used as species-specific evidence for any field, consistent with the scope-discipline rule against genus-generic Eupatorium prose.

records.name_note: Sources split between Purple-headed Sneezeweed and Southern Sneezeweed, both of which NC State's rendered Common Name(s) list stacks, in that order. Missouri Botanical Garden's rendered Common Name field carries exactly one name, 'purple-headed sneezeweed.' On synonymy, NC State renders 'Previously known as:' with three stacked prior names — Helenium floridanum, Helenium godfreyi, Helenium nudiflorum — MoBot's Noteworthy Characteristics prose ends 'Synonymous with H. nudiflorum.', and RHS's dedicated Helenium flexuosum page lists Helenium nudiflorum under Synonyms. Helenium autumnale is landed separately in this catalog as Sneezeweed.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State is the only admissible source carrying a toxicity module for this species. Its page-header warning line reads "This plant has low severity poison characteristics.", and the block itself sits under the Problems value "Poisonous to Humans", so the rating is human-scoped; the page carries no Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tag. Poison Symptoms are given in full as "Salivation, elevated temperature and pulse, with difficulty breathing, vomiting, and convulsions if eaten in large quantities." The Poison Toxic Principle is Sesquiterpene lactone. The full Poison Part list, reproduced without truncation, is Flowers, Leaves and Seeds, each listed as its own item, and the page's Causes Contact Dermatitis field is answered No. NC State also lists Poisonous among the four values of its Plant Type field (Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant, Poisonous, Wildflower) and tags the page #poisonous.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets is left null: the only admissible toxicity source, NC State, scopes its Poison block to "Poisonous to Humans"; no admissible source names cats or dogs specifically for this species, even though the Helenium genus carries a broader livestock-toxicity literature outside these domains.

RHS's dedicated Helenium flexuosum page (rhs.org.uk/plants/139751/helenium-flexuosum/details) supplies only taxonomic and unset fields (Synonyms, Family, Native to GB/Ireland, a genus-level description, Name Status, and a Size section whose only row is 'Time to Maturity: No preference') — it has no populated Sun, Soil, Moisture, Hardiness, or Cultivation sections for this species, so it contributes no cultivation data. Its Genus row ('Helenium may be upright, clump-forming annuals, biennials or herbaceous perennials with simple leaves and showy daisy-like flower-heads over a long period') is genus-level boilerplate and was not read as species text anywhere in this record.

water_regime is left null: NC State and MoBot describe soil-moisture preference ("moist to wet," MoBot's "Water: Medium to wet," "Intolerant of dry soils") but neither gives an explicit watering-frequency/regime instruction distinct from a bare soil-moisture description, so no enum value was assigned.
soil_ph_min/soil_ph_max are left null: no admissible source states a pH band or range for this species.
light_fc_min/light_fc_good are left null: no admissible source gives footcandle figures; only categorical "Full sun" tags were found.

direct_sun_hours_max is left null: NC State's "6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day" phrase is the site-wide Light-category legend text attached to the Full Sun tag, not species-specific prose, so it is excluded per the scope rules.

chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, day_f/night_f range fields, and humidity fields are left null: no admissible source gives a damage-onset temperature, an indoor/outdoor temperature range, or a humidity figure/need for this hardy outdoor perennial. Only USDA hardiness-zone ratings were found (NC State: zones 5a-9b; MoBot: zones 5-9), which are survival-zone ratings, not damage-onset temperatures, and were not used per the rules.

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength are left null: MoBot's Culture section only warns to "Avoid overfertilization, which may cause plants to grow too tall," with no interval, active month, or dilution-strength instruction given.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, and water_estimate_basis are left null: this is an in-ground herbaceous perennial and no admissible source frames its watering in terms of dry-down depth or day intervals.
No admissible source for this species carries an "is often confused with" structured module; none is reported here.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name to lead with. NC State's alphabetized Common Name(s) list stacks "Blue Cardinal Flower," "Great Blue Lobelia," and "Great Lobelia." RHS renders "blue cardinal flower" as the subtitle line beneath its "Lobelia siphilitica" heading, and Missouri Botanical Garden's rendered Common Name field also reads "blue cardinal flower." A dedicated single-species Extension page (University of Maryland Extension) instead uses "Great Blue Lobelia" as its own H1/title for this exact species. Because "Blue Cardinal Flower" collides with the already-landed sibling species Lobelia cardinalis (Cardinal Flower) in this catalog, "Great Blue Lobelia" — the name led by a dedicated single-species page — was chosen as common_name.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State renders its Poison block for this species under the human-scoped heading "Poisonous to Humans:" as separate label/value pairs. Poison Severity is Low. Poison Symptoms are given in full as "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, salivation, exhaustion and weakness, dilation of pupils, convulsions, and coma". The Poison Toxic Principle is "Alkaloids lobelamine, lobeline, and others, plus a volatile oil". The page's Causes Contact Dermatitis field is answered No. The full Poison Part list, reproduced without truncation, is Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Roots, Sap/Juice, Seeds and Stems — seven separately stacked items. NC State also lists Poisonous among the four values of its Plant Type field. RHS's Potentially Harmful field instead reads "Harmful if eaten; skin irritant. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling. Pets: Harmful if eaten; skin irritant. For further information and contact numbers regarding pets, see the HTA guide to potentially harmful plants." The two admissible sources disagree on skin-contact risk: NC State's human Poison block answers Causes Contact Dermatitis No, while RHS calls the plant a skin irritant requiring gloves when handling. RHS's "Pets" line names no specific animal (not scoped to cats or dogs specifically), so per this catalog's toxic_to_pets rule it does not by itself establish pet toxicity.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets left null: the only pet-directed toxicity language found on admissible sources is RHS's unscoped 'Pets: Harmful if eaten; skin irritant' line, which names no specific animal (not cats or dogs specifically) and therefore does not meet this catalog's cat/dog-specific bar. NC State's Poison block for this species is human-scoped and carries no Problem-for-Cats/Problem-for-Dogs tags. A prior landed record (b40) noted that UGA CAES/fieldreport.caes.uga.edu carries a genus-level 'Lobelia spp.' pet-toxicity entry, but that is genus-level, not species-specific, so it was not used here per the single-species-page requirement.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: RHS's only pH field for this species is the categorical 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral,' which explicitly includes alkaline soils as acceptable, so no ceiling or floor can be set from it; NC State carries no pH field for this species at all.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the only hour figures found ('6 or more hours,' '2-6 hours') live inside NC State's site-wide Light-category legend text attached to every species page, not in species-specific prose, so they were not used.

part_sun excluded from outdoor_sun_exposure: UMD's Sun field reads 'Full sun to partial sun,' but the structured sun-exposure fields on both NC State (Full sun / Dappled Sunlight / Partial Shade) and RHS (Full sun, Partial shade) list Partial Shade rather than Partial Sun for this species, so part_sun was left out per the two-of-three structured-field rule.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, humidity_need/pct, light_fc_min/good, water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis, and all fertilize_* fields left null: this is an outdoor, USDA-hardy (NC State: Zones 4a-9b) garden perennial, not a houseplant, and none of the admissible sources frames its temperature, humidity, light-intensity, or watering-interval guidance in the terms these fields ask for. RHS's Cultivation paragraph IS species-specific here — RHS keeps its genus-generic prose in a separately labelled Genus field, and the sibling Lobelia cardinalis page carries different Cultivation, Propagation and Pruning text — but its feeding sentence reads 'Feed every 2 weeks with a balanced liquid fertilizer until midsummer and a low nitrogen fertilizer for the remainder of the growing season.' That is a word-based cadence, not a stated number of days, so fertilize_interval_days was not derived from it per the rule against computing a day-interval from a cadence; fertilize_active_months and fertilize_strength are likewise unstated (no dilution fraction is given).

Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder does carry a dedicated page for this species, at plantfinder.mobot.org/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=i460 (the taxonid lookups tried during research returned unrelated species). It is cited here for soil_drainage, water_regime and name_note. Its multi-name common-name list lives only inside an overlib tooltip and is not quoted; the rendered field is 'Common Name: blue cardinal flower'.

Clemson HGIC (hgic.clemson.edu) and UF/IFAS (edis.ifas.ufl.edu, ask.ifas.ufl.edu) did not yield a dedicated single-species page for Lobelia siphilitica, so they contribute no citations here. Penn State Extension does carry one — extension.psu.edu/rain-garden-plants-great-blue-lobelia, 'Rain Garden Plants: Great Blue Lobelia' — and it is cited above for soil_drainage and water_regime.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name leads. Missouri Botanical Garden's structured Common Name field and RHS's rendered subtitle line (beneath its 'Verbena hastata' heading) both give "American blue vervain," so that is used as common_name here. MoBot's own Noteworthy Characteristics prose nonetheless calls the species "blue vervain," and RHS lists 'blue vervain' only inside its separate Other common names field, which reads "American simpler's joy, blue vervain, ironweed, wild hyssop" — not 'Simpler's Joy' alone, and not 'Swamp Verbena' at all. NC State carries no primary-name field: its Common Name(s) list stacks five entries (Blue Verbena, Blue Vervain, Simpler's Joy, Swamp Verbena, Swamp Vervain) in alphabetical order, the same order as its page-title parenthetical, so that order is alphabetization rather than a ranking. 'Swamp Verbena' and 'Simpler's Joy' are no source's lead name.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets/toxicity_detail left null: no admissible source (NC State, MoBot, RHS) carries a Poison/toxicity module naming cats or dogs for this species. NC State's page has no Poison section or Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags at all. NC State's Ethnobotany field notes swamp vervain 'can, however, interfere with blood pressure medication and hormone therapy, and large doses cause vomiting and diarrhea,' but this is framed around human medicinal use, not pet exposure, so it cannot support toxic_to_pets per the cat/dog-scoping rule.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field also lists 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)' for this species, but RHS's Position field and MoBot's Sun field (the other two admissible structured sun fields) each show only Full sun, so part_shade was left out of outdoor_sun_exposure per the two-of-three rule.

soil_drainage left null. NC State's structured Soil Drainage field renders two separately stacked values, 'Moist' and 'Occasionally Wet', with no well-drained or good-drainage value, and MoBot's structured field reads 'Water: Medium to wet'; both sit at the wet end. RHS's structured Moisture field instead reads 'Moist but well–drained or Well–drained', which is mid-scale. The split is 2-1 toward the wet end rather than a three-way stalemate, but this record applies the two-of-three majority rule only to the structured sun fields, where all three sources carry the same field; here NC State's Soil Drainage tags, MoBot's Water rating and RHS's Moisture field are three different fields on three different scales, and no source states a consistently-wet cultivation requirement, which is what moisture_retentive needs in this catalog. The field is therefore left null rather than resolved by counting heads.

water_regime left null: no admissible source gives an imperative watering statement for this species. MoBot's structured Water field reads 'Medium to wet' (mid-scale per the rule against reading a bare 'Medium' rating as keep_moist), and NC State's Description only describes wild/garden site preference ('moist sites as around ponds, bogs or water'), which is a habitat/landscape-use statement, not a watering instruction.

soil_ph_min/max left null: NC State's page carries no pH field at all. RHS's structured pH field for this species reads 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral,' spanning the entire scale with no ceiling or floor, so no numeric bound can be derived from any admissible source.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the only hour figures found ('6 or more hours' for Full sun, '2-6 hours' for Partial Shade) come from NC State's site-wide light-category legend text embedded in its structured Light field values, not from species-specific prose, per the rule excluding that legend as a source for this field.

day/night temperature fields, humidity fields, light_fc fields, chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, fertilizer fields, and the water day-interval/dry-down fields are all left null: Verbena hastata is treated by every admissible source as an in-ground, outdoor wetland/meadow perennial (NC State Landscape Location: Meadow, Naturalized Area, Pond; RHS suggested planting locations are all outdoor garden types), and none of the three sources frames its care in terms of temperature ranges, humidity percentages, foot-candle light levels, a fertilizing schedule, or a wet/dry-down watering cycle.

RHS's Cultivation paragraph ('Grow in a moist but well-drained moderately fertile soil in full sun') was excluded from every field per the scope-discipline rule: the identical sentence appears verbatim on the RHS page for the sibling cultivar Verbena hastata 'Rosea', confirming it is shared genus/cultivar-group boilerplate rather than species-specific text.

records.name_note: NC State's Common Name(s) list for this species (Allegheny monkey flower, Lavender Musk, Square-stemmed Monkey Flower) is alphabetized and ranks nothing on its own, but 'Allegheny monkey flower' is also the name given first in the page title parenthetical, the name on MoBot's Common Name line, and the common name RHS renders beneath its Plant Profile heading — all three dedicated single-species pages located converge on 'Allegheny monkey flower' as the lead name. MoBot's Noteworthy Characteristics prose additionally gives 'square-stemmed monkey flower' as an alternate common name for the same plant. On the taxonomic-synonymy question: none of the three admissible dedicated-species pages located (NC State, MoBot, RHS) uses the name Erythranthe ringens; all three treat the species under Mimulus ringens, and RHS's Name Status field for that binomial reads 'Correct' with no synonym listed on the page.

chill_damage_f and cool_rest_note left null: no admissible source states a damage-onset temperature or a cool-rest/dormancy note for this species.
day_f_min/max and night_f_min/max left null: no admissible source gives day or night temperature ranges for this outdoor wetland perennial.

humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, light_fc_good left null: no admissible source expresses humidity or footcandle light requirements for this species -- these appear to be houseplant-oriented fields with no supporting content here.

soil_ph_min/soil_ph_max left null: RHS's pH field for this taxon reads 'Acid or Neutral or Alkaline,' i.e. all soil reactions are listed as acceptable, so no ceiling or floor can be set from it; NC State's page for this species does not include a Soil pH field at all.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis left null: this is an in-ground wetland perennial and no admissible source frames its watering in day-interval or dry-down terms.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, fertilize_strength left null: no admissible source addresses fertilizing this species.

MoBot's own structured 'Water: Medium to wet' field was not used alone to support water_regime; the keep_moist determination instead rests on MoBot's species-specific Culture and Uses prose ('grow in moist to wet soils...do not dry out'), which is more specific and was preferred over the coarser structured tag.

hgic.clemson.edu, edis.ifas.ufl.edu, ask.ifas.ufl.edu, extension.psu.edu, extension.umd.edu, and fieldreport.caes.uga.edu were considered but no dedicated single-species Mimulus ringens (or Erythranthe ringens) page could be located on those domains within this session's search budget; only plants.ces.ncsu.edu, plantfinder.mobot.org and rhs.org.uk yielded usable species-specific pages, and no field in this record relies on the other listed domains. The MoBot URL captured during research (PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286977&isprofile=1&basic=Allegheny%20monkey%20flower) serves Asplenium platyneuron, not this species; every MoBot quote in this record was re-pointed at the dedicated Mimulus ringens page, PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=z410, on which the auditor verified each one verbatim.

scientific_name_accepted stays Mimulus ringens. No admissible source located uses the name Erythranthe ringens for this species: the string does not occur on NC State's page or RHS's, NC State's current page title is 'Mimulus ringens', and RHS's Name Status for that binomial reads Correct with no synonym block. Some sources outside this catalog's closed domain list now file the species under Erythranthe; that could not be checked against an admissible page and is disclosed here rather than followed.

records.name_note: Both admissible sources use the same accepted binomial: RHS's dedicated page for Thalictrum pubescens Pursh gives Name Status Correct, and Missouri Botanical Garden's page heads the same taxon Thalictrum pubescens; no source disputes it. RHS additionally lists Thalictrum polygamum and Thalictrum revolutum under Synonyms, so RHS treats material published under those names as this taxon. The two pages differ on which vernacular they designate as primary: RHS's plant-profile subtitle reads 'tall meadow rue' and its Other common names field adds 'muskrat weed, musquash weed, quicksilver weed, rattlesnake bite, shining grass', while Missouri Botanical Garden's Common Name field reads 'Common Name: thalictrum', the genus-level umbrella term, with 'commonly known as tall meadow rue' appearing only in its Noteworthy Characteristics prose. common_name is taken from RHS's subtitle, the only species-specific primary designation of the two. Neither dedicated page uses the alternate English name 'King of the Meadow'.
unknowns: No admissible source provides cat/dog toxicity information for Thalictrum pubescens. NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox has no dedicated page for this species (https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/thalictrum-pubescens/ returns 404, and site search surfaces only sibling species pages such as T. dasycarpum, T. dioicum, and T. amphibolum), so its Poison/Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags could not be checked for this taxon. toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null rather than borrowed from a related species.

Clemson HGIC's Meadow Rue page (hgic.clemson.edu/meadow-rue) is a genus-level article discussing Thalictrum rochebruneanum 'Lavender Mist' and T. flavum subsp. glaucum, not a dedicated Thalictrum pubescens page, so it was excluded as a source for species-specific fields per the single-species-page rule.

RHS's dedicated page for this species (Thalictrum pubescens Pursh) is a thin profile carrying only Family, Native-to-GB/Ireland, a genus-level description, Name Status, and Synonyms/Other-common-names fields. It has no Hardiness rating, Position/Aspect, Soil, Moisture, or Toxicity section for this species (unlike cultivar pages such as 'Purple Haze'), so hardiness-derived and RHS soil/sun/toxicity fields are left null rather than taken from a sibling cultivar page.

No admissible source frames this in-ground perennial in indoor terms, so day/night temperature, humidity, light_fc, direct_sun_hours_max, chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, soil pH and all fertilize_* fields are left null. is_houseplant is false, inferred from the consistent outdoor cultivation picture on the one source that carries cultivation fields for this species: Missouri Botanical Garden's Type ('Herbaceous perennial'), Zone ('3 to 8') and Uses ('Good tall selection for rear of beds and borders.').

Clemson HGIC (hgic.clemson.edu) returned no matches for Carex stricta in site-restricted search. UF/IFAS EDIS and Ask IFAS searches returned no dedicated Carex stricta page. Penn State Extension and University of Maryland Extension results were multi-species PDFs (native plant lists) rather than dedicated single-species pages, and the UGA CAES Field Report result was a multi-species grasses-and-sedges guide; per the single-species-page requirement, none of these were used for any claim.

RHS carries a dedicated page for 'Carex stricta Lam.' (Name Status: Correct) used only to confirm scientific_name_accepted; it has no cultivation, common-name, or sun/soil data. A separate RHS page for 'Carex stricta Gooden.' is marked Name Status: Synonym with Plant Range: Europe to Iran -- a different, non-North-American taxonomic concept -- and was not used for any claim. Other RHS results (e.g. Carex stricta 'Aurea', 'Bowles's Variety', 'Sue Ward') are cultivar pages, excluded per the dedicated-single-species-page rule.

outdoor_sun_exposure is limited to full_sun and part_shade per MoBot's literal structured Sun field ('Full sun to part shade'); part_sun is not listed because it is not explicitly named. Shade appears twice in the prose — the Culture paragraph's tolerance aside 'Tolerates shady conditions.' and the Uses paragraph's 'Ground cover for shady areas.' — but the structured Sun field bounds the range at part shade, so full_shade is not added.

MoBot's structured Water field reads 'Water: Medium to wet' -- broader than the bare 'Medium' the rules flag as mid-scale-only; this is treated as consistent with (not contradicting) the keep_moist call drawn from the Uses paragraph's explicit 'kept consistently moist' language.

records.name_note: NC State's rendered Common Name(s) list leads with 'Woolgrass', with 'Woolgrass Bulrush' second, and Missouri Botanical Garden's Noteworthy Characteristics prose says the species is 'commonly called woolgrass'; MoBot's own structured Common Name field, however, renders the two-word form 'wool grass', so the one-word spelling this record lands appears in MoBot's prose rather than in its designated field. University of Maryland Extension's dedicated page is titled 'Wool Rush or Wool Grass'. RHS leads with a different name entirely: 'cotton grass' is the subtitle line directly under its 'Scirpus cyperinus' heading, and its Other common names field renders 'cotton grass, wool grass', so wool grass is the second, non-lead entry there. Three of the four sources therefore lead with a wool-prefixed name and 'Woolgrass' is NC State's lead, which is the form landed here. Separately, despite the '-grass' in most of these common names, MoBot's Noteworthy Characteristics prose and UMD's structured field both classify the plant in the sedge family (Cyperaceae), not true grasses.
unknowns: No admissible source presents a numeric chill-damage onset temperature; NC State lists only a USDA hardiness zone range (4a-8b), which is a survival/hardiness rating, not a damage-onset temperature, so chill_damage_f is left null.

No admissible source gives day/night temperature ranges, humidity percentages, or light foot-candle values for this outdoor wetland perennial, so day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, and light_fc_good are left null.

direct_sun_hours_max is left null: the only hour figures found are inside NC State's site-wide Light-category legend parentheticals ('6 or more hours', '2-6 hours'), which the rules exclude as generic legend text rather than species-specific prose.

soil_drainage is left null: NC State's Soil Drainage tags (Moist, Occasionally Dry, Occasionally Wet) span both the occasionally-dry and occasionally-wet bands, which maps to 'moderate,' but MoBot's structured Water field ('Wet'), MoBot's Culture text ('moist to wet soils including shallow standing water'), and UMD's Soil field ('Moist to wet soils of any texture') all describe consistently wet conditions, closer to 'moisture_retentive.' The admissible sources genuinely disagree, so the field is left null.
soil_ph_min/max are left null: only UMD Extension gives a descriptive pH range ('acidic to neutral') with no numeric values, and no other admissible source states a pH figure for this species.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, and water_dormant_days_est are left null: this is an in-ground wetland perennial sedge, and none of the admissible sources frame its watering in terms of a dry-down depth or day-interval schedule.

No admissible source discusses fertilizing this species (interval, active months, or strength); NC State and MoBot both describe it as low-maintenance with no serious insect or disease problems, so fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength are left null.
No admissible source (NC State, MoBot, RHS, or UMD) mentions toxicity to cats, dogs, or any other animal for this species, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null.
cool_rest_note is left null: no admissible source frames a cool/dormancy rest period for this species beyond noting that foliage and seed heads remain attractive through winter.

RHS's dedicated page for this species carries no Cultivation, Position, Soil, or hardiness-rating (e.g. 'H' code) fields beyond Name Status and Size/Time to Maturity, so it could not be used for any cultivation-related field.

A UF/IFAS dedicated single-species page for Scirpus cyperinus does exist (plant-directory.ifas.ufl.edu/plant-directory/scirpus-cyperinus/, UF/IFAS Center for Aquatic and Invasive Plants), but it carries only habitat and morphology prose — no light, water, soil, pH or toxicity fields — so it changes no landed value; it adds a fourth common-name variant, 'wool-grass', which does not displace NC State's lead 'Woolgrass'. No Clemson HGIC or UGA CAES dedicated single-species page was located, and Penn State's only hit is a multi-species pocket guide, excluded as non-dedicated. NC State, MoBot, RHS and UMD Extension are the admissible dedicated single-species pages used here.

normalizations: 2026-09-10: b76 landed by a second session (branch claude/database-build-goals-e548af). Eight native wet-meadow perennials: American Boneset, Purple-headed Sneezeweed, Great Blue Lobelia, American Blue Vervain, Allegheny Monkey Flower, Tall Meadow Rue, Tussock Sedge, Woolgrass. Auditor-supplied corrected wording used verbatim where the audit gave a whole string; every reachable citation substitute was ground-truthed with qc.py before being applied. Landing decisions: Eupatorium perfoliatum's soil_drainage came back moisture_retentive and lands moderate — its only wet-side evidence is Penn State's rain-garden Site Conditions labels ('needs constant moisture', 'Hydrologic zones: Wet/moist') and a flood-tolerance sentence, while NC State's Soil Drainage field pairs Good Drainage with Moist, NC State's Description reads 'average, medium to wet' and RHS's Moisture field reads 'Moist but well–drained or Poorly–drained' (the b54 rule: a rain-garden siting label is not a cultivation drainage requirement). Lobelia siphilitica's soil_drainage was nulled on audit for resting on RHS alone and is restored as moisture_retentive on NC State's Soil Drainage field (Moist, Occasionally Wet, no well-drained value) plus MoBot's Culture requirement 'Needs constant moisture.'; MoBot (kempercode=i460) and Penn State's Great Blue Lobelia page, which the research pass reported as non-existent, were worked in. All six Mimulus ringens MoBot citations were re-pointed from taxonid=286977 (which serves Asplenium platyneuron) to the correct kempercode=z410 page; Mimulus ringens is kept as scientific_name_accepted on RHS's Name Status Correct and NC State's current page title, with the Erythranthe reclassification disclosed as unverifiable against the closed source list. Thalictrum pubescens and Carex stricta landed is_houseplant null and land false, on MoBot's Type, Zone, Uses and Suggested Use fields. Five common names were title-cased or moved to a dedicated page's lead: Boneset -> American Boneset, Purplehead Sneezeweed -> Purple-headed Sneezeweed, Blue Vervain -> American Blue Vervain, Allegheny Monkeyflower -> Allegheny Monkey Flower, tussock sedge -> Tussock Sedge. Poison-block citations that glued an NC State label to its value ('Poison Severity: Low', 'Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes/No') were re-quoted as the value alone, and Great Blue Lobelia's five-field semicolon-joined poison synthesis was split into one citation per rendered field. Two Penn State quotes carrying a stray pipe ('Soil:| Clay and sandy...') were re-quoted from the page. verify_quotes: every reachable quote verified after repair; MoBot pages skipped from this machine (ConnectError).
